eventMetadata.context_description: Traders have concentrated bets on 36°C and 37°C as the highest temperature in Manila on May 25, reflecting the tail end of the hot dry season when daytime maxima typically peak near 34–36°C under strong solar heating and urban heat-island effects. Recent PAGASA observations recorded 36.4°C, while long-range outlooks show highs of 34–37°C (93–98°F) before afternoon easterly-driven cloud build-up and isolated thunderstorms moderate further warming. Model guidance indicates modest variability from these factors—clearer skies could push readings to 37°C, whereas increased moisture and convective activity favor 35–36°C—creating the tight spread between the top outcomes. Updated regional forecasts and 48-hour model runs will provide the next key data points before resolution.
